To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
There were no causal genetic associations between later life cognitive abilities and physical health, and between educational attainment and physical health.
there was no evidence for causal associations from cognitive ability to physical health, or from educational attainment to health.

there is no evidence of a causal association between cognitive ability, as measured by later life cognitive ability tests, and physical health, and that there is no causal association between educational attainment (a proxy for cognitive ability), and physical health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the causal genetic associations of physical health and cognitive ability.
a potential genetic basis to the association between cognitive function and health.
the causes of the association between physical health and cognitive ability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic associations between cognitive function and physical health are weak and inconsistent, but that this may not be the case for non-genetic causal associations.

the genetic evidence is consistent with no causal association between cognitive ability, education attainment, and health, although this may be because the genetic instruments are not sufficiently powerful to detect such effects.
the genetic evidence for a shared genetic aetiologic mechanism between cognitive ability, education, and physical health is weak.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no clear causal associations between cognitive abilities and physical health.
the genetic evidence does not suggest causal associations between cognitive function and health.
the genetic architecture for cognitive ability and educational attainment is not the same as the genetic architecture for the physical health traits we examined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic evidence is consistent with the hypothesis that physical health and cognitive ability are causally independent.
the genetic architecture of the associations between cognitive ability (and educational attainment) and physical health is complex, with many genes of small effect.
there is little evidence for a causal role of cognitive ability or educational attainment in influencing physical health.
